items.title: Antonelli's drivers' title is settled; Mercedes still chasing constructors' crown
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli clinched the Drivers' Championship in Mexico. The latest official standings show 380 points for Antonelli and 261 for Verstappen; Mercedes leads Ferrari 630-504. Formula1.com's pre-weekend scenario says Mercedes seals the constructors' title if it gains three points on Ferrari in Brazil.
items.why_it_matters: Brazil's practice has not changed the standings, and the constructors' title remains undecided. These are current pre-race totals, not a result projection.

items.title: Norris edges Antonelli and Verstappen to top Brazil FP1
items.summary: The official 22-car Practice 1 classification has Lando Norris first in 1:11.717, 0.082s ahead of Kimi Antonelli, with Max Verstappen third at +0.236s. The Race also reports that Colton Herta completed the 100km needed for his final Super Licence point.
items.why_it_matters: This was the first practice session only; its order awards no points and is not a forecast of qualifying or the Grand Prix. Herta's licence eligibility does not confirm a 2027 seat.

items.title: FIA confirms Russell's five-place grid drop for sixth ICE
items.summary: Document 14 recorded Russell's sixth ICE against four allowed and the Technical Delegate's non-compliance finding. The Stewards' separate Document 15 now imposes a five-place drop for the next race in which he participates.
items.why_it_matters: Document 14 is the technical report; Document 15 is the sanction. Keeping them separate avoids treating the earlier report as the penalty decision.

sources.label: FIA: Russell PU change, Stewards' Document 15

items.title: McLaren brings four declared car updates to Interlagos
items.summary: FIA Document 12 lists McLaren changes to the front wing, rear wing, beam wing and floor furniture; the other ten teams submitted nil returns. The Race reports that the new front-wing concept is intended to carry into McLaren's 2027 launch specification.
items.why_it_matters: These are team-declared components and design aims, not independently measured performance gains. The FIA page-3 diagram accompanies the declaration.

sources.label: The Race: McLaren's Brazil upgrades and 2027 front wing

items.title: Colapinto fined after FP1 pit-lane speeding
items.summary: The Stewards' Document 16 records Franco Colapinto at 80.6 km/h in the 80 km/h pit lane and fines BWT Alpine F1 Team EUR 100. Separate Document 18 lists lap-time deletions for ten drivers at turns 1, 7, 10 and 12.
items.why_it_matters: The fine applies to the team. The listed lap deletions are not additional race penalties or changes to the official FP1 classification.

sources.label: FIA: FP1 deleted lap times, Document 18
